text.p: Newly-floated Halifax Building Society said on Monday the average price of an auction of around 570 million shares by members was 732.5 pence per share.
Halifax's brokers Merrill Lynch and Cazenove auctioned 23 percent of its flotation shares on Friday to institutional investors.
Halifax had guaranteed shareholders selling their entitlement at auction would receive at least 415 pence per share.
It said in a statement that the auction range was 710 pence to 815 pence per share.

Analysts said this auction would have seen aggressive bidding from institutions which missed out on the strong early performance of another building society, the Alliance & Leicester, when it floated last month.
Halifax also announced that it has received orders to sell 0.4 percent of the company's issued share capital in its first daily tender. Bids in the tender will be accepted up to 1800 GMT today.
Until now Halifax, like Britain's other building societies, has been owned by its savers and borrowers -- known as its members.
